questions.question: Rickets is caused by deficiency of:
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**vitamin D**__

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Rickets** is a condition that affects bone development in children. It causes the bones to become soft and weak, which can lead to bone deformities.
 
• The primary cause of rickets is a **deficiency of vitamin D**.
 
• Vitamin D is essential for the absorption of calcium and phosphate from the diet, which are critical for healthy bone formation.
 
• Without sufficient vitamin D, the body cannot properly regulate calcium and phosphate levels, leading to the symptoms of rickets.
 
• Common sources of vitamin D include exposure to sunlight, which triggers vitamin D production in the skin, and dietary sources such as fatty fish, liver, and fortified foods.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• Rickets can also be caused by genetic factors, certain medical conditions, or malabsorption disorders that affect the body's ability to process vitamin D.
 
• Preventing rickets involves ensuring adequate intake of vitamin D through diet and supplementation, as well as sensible sun exposure.
 
• Treatment for rickets typically includes vitamin D and calcium supplements, and in severe cases, corrective surgery may be required to address bone deformities.
 
• Public health measures, such as fortifying foods with vitamin D, have been effective in reducing the incidence of rickets in many parts of the world.

__
 
• The human **eye** loses its power of accommodation at old age.
 
• The ability of the eye to focus on both, near and distant objects, by adjusting its focal length, is called the accommodation of the eye.
 
• The muscles in our eye can adjust the focus of the lens present in our eye to focus on different objects at different times at different distances.
 
• Due to this ability, our eye can focus on near as well as far away objects, and this ability is called the **power of accommodation. **
 
• The maximum power of accommodation of the eye for a person having **normal vision (d = 25 cm) is 4 Dioptre.**

** [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] Additional Information__**Diseases associated with eyes:

 
• Myopia- The human eye can see a nearby object clearly but cannot see far away object clearly.
 
• Hypermetropia- The human eye can see distant objects clearly but cannot see nearby objects clearly.
 
• Presbyopia- In this defect, both near and far objects are not clearly visible. It is an old age disease and it is due to the losing power of accommodation.
 
• Astigmatism- In this defect, the eye cannot see horizontal and vertical lines clearly, simultaneously. It is due to the imperfect spherical nature of the eye lens.

questions.question: Constipation could be a sign that the person in suffering from a lack of ___________.
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Dietary Fibre**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• Dietary fibre is essential for maintaining a healthy digestive system and aids in regular bowel movements by increasing stool bulk.
 
• A lack of dietary fibre can lead to constipation, as the body struggles to efficiently pass stool through the intestines.
 
• Sources of dietary fibre include fruits (e.g., apples, bananas), vegetables (e.g., broccoli, carrots), whole grains (e.g., oats, brown rice), legumes, and seeds.
 
• The recommended daily intake of fibre for adults is approximately 25-30 grams, depending on gender and age, according to global health standards.
 
• Dietary fibre also helps regulate blood sugar levels and cholesterol, making it beneficial for overall health beyond digestion.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Types of Dietary Fibre:**

• **Insoluble fibre:** Does not dissolve in water; helps add bulk to stool; found in whole grains, nuts, and vegetables.

questions.question: Which condition, also known as icterus, causes a yellowing of your skin and the whites of your eyes?

__
 
• **Jaundice (Icterus)** is a condition where the skin, the whites of the eyes (sclera), and sometimes other tissues develop a yellow tint.
 
• This yellowing happens because of an excessive buildup of a substance called **bilirubin** in the blood.
 
• Bilirubin is a yellow pigment produced during the normal breakdown of red blood cells.
 
• Normally, the liver processes bilirubin and excretes it into bile, which helps digest fats.
 
• The bile is then eliminated from the body through stool.
 
• Causes of Jaundice
 
 
• Pre-hepatic (before the liver):
 
• Caused by increased destruction of red blood cells (hemolysis).
 
• Examples: Sickle cell anaemia, malaria.
 
• Hepatic (in the liver):
 
• Caused by liver diseases that impair its ability to process bilirubin.
 
• Examples: Hepatitis, cirrhosis, alcoholic liver disease.
 
• Post-hepatic (after the liver):
 
• Caused by an obstruction in bile ducts that prevents bilirubin from being excreted.
 
• Examples: Gallstones, tumors, bile duct strictures.
 
 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

• It’s commonly triggered by allergens, irritants, or stress.

• The body’s immune system mistakenly attacks the proteins that hold skin cells together.

• **Ebola:** Transmitted to humans through contact with blood, secretions, organs, or other bodily fluids of infected animals.

• **Avian Influenza:** Commonly known as bird flu, it is a viral infection that can infect not only birds but also humans and other animals.

• **Public Health Measures:**
 
 
• Preventive measures include wearing masks, practicing hand hygiene, and maintaining physical distance.
 
• Controlling zoonotic diseases involves monitoring animal health, regulating wildlife trade, and ensuring food safety.

questions.question: Organisms such as bacteria, viruses, fungi, protozoans, helminths, etc., that cause diseases in humans are called ______.
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**pathogens.**__

__
 
• A** pathogen **is an **organism that causes disease.**
 
• **Pathogens **can be **transmitted **in a few ways depending on the type.
 
• They can be **spread through skin contact, bodily fluids, airborne particles, **contact with feces, etc.
 
• There are **different types of pathogens **out of which the **four most common types **are viruses, bacteria, fungi, and parasites.
 
 
• **Viruses **are made up of a piece of** genetic code, **such as **DNA or RNA**, and **protected by a coating of a protein called a capsid.**
 
• **Bacteria **are **microorganisms **made of a **single cell **and those **bacteria **which **cause infection **are called **pathogenic bacteria.**
 
• **Fungi **cells contain a **nucleus and other components **protected by a membrane and a **thick cell wall.**
 
 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Parasites **are organisms that behave like tiny animals, **living in or on a host **and **feeding from the host**. It includes:

 
 
• **Protozoa** are **single-celled organisms **that can **live and multiply in the body.**
 
• **Helminths** are **larger, multi-celled organisms **that can **live inside or outside **the body and are commonly **known as worms**.
 
 
 
• **Predators **are animals that **kill and eat other animals.**
 
• **Antigens **are **substance that enters the body **and starts **a process that can cause disease**.
 
• The **body **then **usually produces substances (antibodies) **to fight the antigens.
 
• **Frugivores **are animal that **feeds on fruit.**

• These diseases progress gradually and usually end up causing long-term damage to organs and internal systems. sometimes chronic diseases become fatal and cause **loss of life.**
 
• Examples of Chronic diseases are **Diabetes, cancer, tuberculosis, arthritis, etc.**

__
 
• **Dengue viruses **are spread to people through the bites of infected **Aedes species mosquitoes**. These are the same types of mosquitoes that spread** Zika** and **chikungunya viruses**.
 
• These mosquitoes typically lay eggs near standing water in containers that hold water, like **buckets, bowls, animal dishes, flower pots**, and **vases**.
 
• These **mosquitoes** prefer to bite people, and live both** indoors** and **outdoors** near people.
 
• **Mosquitoes **that spread dengue, chikungunya, and Zika bite during the day and night.
 
• Mosquitoes become infected when they bite a person infected with the virus. Infected mosquitoes can then spread the virus to other people through bites.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• A disease is an infection or an abnormal condition that negatively affects the structure and capacity of all parts or in particular specific parts of organisms.
 
• It is not due to the immediate physical injury. 
 
• Infections are frequently known to be ailments that are related to explicit signs and side effects.
 
• There are different types of diseases such as: 
 
 
• Infectious diseases
 
• Deficiency diseases
 
• Hereditary diseases 
 
• Physiological diseases 
 
 
 
• ​Diseases can also be classified into Communicable and Non-communicable diseases. 
 
• It can spread through the direct transfer of bacteria, viruses, or other germs from one person to another or through mosquito bites, etc.
 
• **Diarrhoea **is usually a symptom of an infection in the intestinal tract, which can be caused by a variety of bacterial, viral and parasitic organisms. Infection is spread through contaminated food or drinking-water, or from person-to-person as a result of poor hygiene.
 
• **Elephantiasis** refers to a parasitic infection that causes extreme swelling in the arms and legs. The disease is caused by the filarial worm, Wuchereria bancrofti which is transmitted from human to human via the female mosquito when it takes a blood meal.
 
• **Malaria** is caused by the Plasmodium parasite. The parasite is spread to humans through the bites of infected mosquitoes.

questions.question: Down Syndrome, which causes learning difficulties and physical health development delays and disabilities, is a:
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**genetic disease**__.

__
 
• **Down Syndrome is a genetic disease**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

 
• **Down syndrome** is a genetic condition that arises** due to the presence of an extra chromosome 21.**

 
 
• Here, chromosome 21 is repeated thrice (trisomy 21), instead of showing up twice in a normal individual.
 
• The karyotype of Down syndrome is represented as 47, XX, +21 (females) and 47, XY, +21 (males)
 
• **Some of the most common are characteristics of down syndrome:**
 
 
• Flat face, round head, and typical epicanthic fold of the eyes
 
• Short, broad hands
 
• Mental retardation Hypotonia – poor muscle tone
 
• Short stature
 
• Protruding furrowed tongue
 
• Chromosomal Aberrations
 
• Mild to moderate developmental disabilities
 
• Typical dermatoglyphic patterns (palm and fingerprint patterns)
 
 
 
 
 
• Recognizing the need to support people suffering from Down Syndrome, the WHO **on 20th December 2007, recognised March 21st as ‘World Down Syndrome Day’.**

questions.question: Which disease is caused by iron deficiency?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Anemia**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• Anemia __is caused due to deficiency of Iron.
 
• Anemia, also spelled Anaemia, is usually characterized as a decrease in the total amount of red blood cells (RBCs) or hemoglobin in the blood which mainly contains Iron as a significant body mineral.
 
• It can also be defined as the blood's ability to carry oxygen to decrease.
 
• As anemia gradually progresses, the symptoms are often unclear and can include feeling tired, fatigue, shortness of breath, or poor exercise capacity.
 
• Anemia that develops rapidly also has greater symptoms, which can include confusion, feeling one passing out, losing consciousness, or thirst. Until a person is visibly pale anemia has to be significant.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

 
• **Thyroid**

 
 
• The thyroid gland produces hormones that regulate the body's metabolic rate-controlling heart, muscle, and digestive function, brain development, and bone maintenance. Controlling metabolism is the main function of the thyroid gland.
 
 
 
• **Hypocalcemia**
 
 
• A condition in which the blood has too little calcium.
 
• 
 
It can be caused by a lack of vitamin D. It can also signal a condition of the four small glands in the neck (the parathyroid glands), the kidneys or the pancreas

 
 
 
 
• **Kwashiorkor**
 
 
• Lack of protein in the diet causes Kwashiorkor. Protein is found in every cell of the human body.
 
• Protein is needed in the human body's diet to repair and regenerate cells.
 
• This is how a healthy human body regenerates cells on a regular basis.
 
• Protein is particularly necessary for growth in children and during pregnancy.
 
• When the body is deficient in protein, growth and regular bodily functions slow down, and kwashiorkor develops.
 
• Proteins are in charge of keeping the body's fluid balance.
 
• Inadequate protein causes fluid to migrate to parts of the body where it shouldn't be, accumulating in the tissues.
 
• Fluid retention, often known as edoema, is caused by a fluid imbalance across the walls of capillaries.

__
 
• ** Hepatitis is a viral infection that affects the liver and can cause inflammation and damage to the liver.**
 
• There are different types of hepatitis viruses, such as hepatitis **A, B, C, D, and E,** and each is transmitted in different ways.
 
• **Hepatitis A and E** are usually transmitted through contaminated food or water, and they do not cause chronic liver disease.
 
• Hepatitis** B, C, and D** are transmitted through infected **blood or body fluids, and they can cause chronic liver disease and lead to liver failure or liver cancer.**
 
• **Mosquitoes, **on the other hand, are known to transmit various diseases such as malaria, dengue fever, Zika virus, and yellow fever, but they do not transmit hepatitis viruses.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• ** Elephantiasis** is a parasitic infection that is transmitted by mosquitoes and causes chronic swelling and enlargement of body parts due to damage to the lymphatic system.

 
 
• It can be prevented through measures such as mosquito control and proper treatment of infected individuals.
 
 
 
• **Dengue** is a viral infection that is transmitted to humans by infected mosquitoes, primarily the Aedes aegypti mosquito.
 
 
• It is a common mosquito-borne disease that is prevalent in tropical and subtropical regions of the world.
 
 
 
• 
 
**Malaria** is a serious and sometimes fatal disease caused by a parasite called Plasmodium, which is transmitted to humans through the bites of infected female Anopheles mosquitoes.

 
 
• 
 
Malaria is most prevalent in tropical and subtropical regions of the world, including many countries in Africa, Asia, and the Americas.
